data.name: Australia
data.summary: Australian residents are taxed on worldwide income at up to 45% plus the 2% Medicare levy (47%) above AUD 190,000. Capital gains on assets held 12 months get a 50% discount, so the top effective rate is 23.5%; the May 2026 Budget announced that from 1 July 2027 the discount will be replaced by inflation indexation with a 30% minimum tax on post-July-2027 gains (announced, legislative status not verified). Franked Australian dividends carry a 30% imputation credit (net top rate about 24.3% of the cash dividend); foreign dividends are taxed at up to 47% with a foreign tax offset. There is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax; assets inherited by residents keep the deceased's cost base, but CGT can be triggered when assets pass to non-resident beneficiaries. Holders of temporary visas are exempt on most foreign income and gains.

regimes.name: Australian tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation at resident rates (2026/27: 45% above AUD 190,000) plus 2% Medicare levy.
regimes.eligibility: Resident under the domicile test, the 183-day test or ordinary concepts; permanent residents and citizens are taxed on worldwide income.

capital_gains.summary: Net capital gains are added to taxable income. Individuals who hold an asset at least 12 months get a 50% discount (for disposals up to 30 June 2027), so the top effective rate is 47% x 50% = 23.5%. Gains on assets held under 12 months are taxed at up to 47%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Main residence exemption; pre-CGT assets (acquired before 20 September 1985) exempt until 30 June 2027. Small business CGT concessions for active business assets (not modelled).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Budget 2026-27 (12 May 2026): from 1 July 2027 the 50% discount is replaced by cost-base indexation and a 30% minimum tax on capital gains arising after 1 July 2027; pre-CGT assets become taxable; investors in new builds may choose the old discount. Not yet in force; legislative status not verified. Ceasing residence is a CGT event (I1) on non-Australian assets (general rule, not verified from an opened source in this session).

sources.title: Australia - Individual - Taxes on personal income

capital_gains.rate_basis: Top marginal rate 45% + 2% Medicare levy = 47%; 50% CGT discount for assets held at least 12 months gives 23.5%. Law in force for disposals to 30 June 2027; from 1 July 2027 post-2027 gains are expected to bear indexation plus a 30% minimum tax (higher for most large gains). Private business before small business concessions.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Share traders are taxed on revenue account (gains fully assessable at up to 47%, no discount); classification follows the facts (frequency, organisation, profit intention).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: At least 12 months for the 50% discount.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains taxable; foreign income tax offset available. Temporary residents are exempt on assets that are not taxable Australian property.

dividends.summary: Franked dividends from Australian companies are grossed up for the company tax paid (up to 30%) and the franking credit is offset against personal tax, with excess refundable. A top-rate individual pays 47% on the grossed-up amount less the 30% credit, i.e. about 24.3% of the cash dividend. Foreign dividends are taxed at up to 47% with a foreign income tax offset for source withholding.
dividends.important_exceptions: Controlled foreign company rules can attribute passive income of foreign companies controlled by Australians.
dividends.rate_basis: Fully franked dividend D: taxable D/0.7, tax 47% x D/0.7 = 0.671D less franking credit 0.429D = 0.243D (24.3% of cash). Foreign dividends: 47% before foreign income tax offset.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on franked dividends; unfranked dividends 30% (15% for most treaty residents), exempt to the extent declared conduit foreign income.
dividends.treaty_network: About 50 treaties listed by PwC, including the United States (15% portfolio dividends).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 30% (25% for base rate entities with turnover under AUD 50 million and passive income no more than 80%). The usual family vehicle, a discretionary trust streaming dividends to a 30% 'bucket company' and capital gains to individuals, is modelled as the 'family_trust_bucket_company' structure regime.

wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Division 296: per PwC, from 1 July 2026 individuals with total superannuation balances above AUD 3 million pay an extra 15% on earnings attributable to the balance between AUD 3 million and 10 million and 25% above AUD 10 million. This is an earnings tax on superannuation, not a wealth tax; it matters only to families with large super balances.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: State land tax on the unimproved value of land (principal residence exempt; thresholds vary), council rates, stamp duty on purchases, and foreign purchaser surcharges on duty and land tax in several states. A federal annual vacancy fee applies to foreign-owned vacant dwellings. Foreign persons, including temporary residents, are banned from buying established dwellings until 30 June 2029 (limited exceptions).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. When a resident beneficiary inherits, any CGT is generally deferred: the beneficiary takes over the deceased's cost base (or market value for pre-CGT assets and certain main residences) and pays CGT only on a later sale. CGT is triggered at death when an asset passes to a non-resident beneficiary or a tax-advantaged entity (CGT event K3), apart from taxable Australian property. Gifts are a disposal by the donor at market value, so a gift of appreciated shares to a child triggers CGT (23.5% at the top rate).
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: No tax of any amount on inheritances to children.
inheritance.regional_differences: Probate fees are set by each state's Supreme Court and are modest in absolute terms (not verified).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Superannuation death benefits paid to adult (non-dependant) children are taxed (rates not verified here). The K3 rule makes leaving shares to a child who lives abroad a taxable event.
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax; a gift is a CGT disposal at market value by the donor.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No inheritance tax on any assets.

regimes.name: Temporary resident (temporary visa holder)
regimes.description: Holders of temporary visas who are not Social Security Act residents and have no Australian-resident spouse are exempt from Australian tax on foreign-source income and on capital gains on assets that are not taxable Australian property. No current visa lets a non-working wealthy family live in Australia on a temporary basis, so this regime is effectively unavailable; it is kept only as a low-confidence placeholder.
regimes.eligibility: Hold a temporary visa under the Migration Act 1958; not an Australian resident for Social Security Act purposes; spouse not an Australian resident under that Act. No realistic visa exists today for a non-working wealthy family. Home Affairs states that the Business Innovation and Investment Program (subclass 188, including the Significant Investor stream) is closed as of 31 July 2024. The National Innovation visa (subclass 858) is a permanent visa ('Permanently' per Home Affairs), so holders are ordinary residents and the exemption does not apply. Every other temporary visa requires work, study or sponsorship (e.g. the Skills in Demand visa needs genuine employment by an approved sponsor). The only temporary visa open without those conditions is the Visitor visa (subclass 600), granted for stays of 3, 6 or 12 months and not meant for living in Australia; duration is therefore set to 1 year as a placeholder. Eligible citizenships are restricted to OTHER as an empty-safe choice: in practice only New Zealand citizens (Special Category visa, subclass 444, no fixed term) can live in Australia indefinitely on a temporary visa without working, and they fall in OTHER. EU and US families cannot use this regime.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on foreign assets (anything that is not taxable Australian property, e.g. foreign listed shares and portfolio holdings of Australian shares under 10%) are disregarded. Gains on Australian real estate and other taxable Australian property are taxed as for residents (23.5% with the discount; temporary residents may lose the discount for periods of non-residence).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Temporary visa; not a Social Security Act resident; no Australian-resident spouse. No visa route exists for a non-working wealthy family (BIIP closed 31 July 2024; National Innovation visa is permanent), so this regime is a placeholder restricted to OTHER (New Zealand citizens on a subclass 444 visa) with a 1-year visitor-visa duration.

regimes.name: Discretionary family trust with a corporate beneficiary ('bucket company')
regimes.description: The portfolio is held by a discretionary (family) trust with a company as trustee. Each year the trustee streams capital gains to individual family members, who keep the 50% CGT discount (23.5% at the top rate, less for adult children on lower incomes), and streams dividends and other income to a family-owned 'bucket' company taxed at a flat 30%. Foreign dividends therefore bear 30% instead of up to 47%, and franked Australian dividends bear no extra tax in the company. Tax on the bucket company's profits is deferred until it pays franked dividends to the family. Law in force for 2026; the May 2026 Budget announced a 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts from 1 July 2028 and the end of the CGT discount for gains after 1 July 2027, which would largely remove the advantage.
regimes.eligibility: Any Australian-resident family (the trust and company must be Australian resident). Not suitable for US persons: for US tax the trust is a foreign non-grantor trust and the company a PFIC/CFC, with punitive results. Temporary residents gain little, because their foreign income is already exempt.
regimes.duration_note: No statutory limit on the structure; a discretionary trust lasts until its vesting date, normally up to 80 years under state perpetuity law (South Australia has no limit). The advantage depends on the 2026 law: the announced 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts (from 1 July 2028) and CGT changes (from 1 July 2027) are not modelled.

structure.entity: Discretionary family trust (corporate trustee) plus a private 'bucket' company as beneficiary
structure.payout_notes: Capital gains streamed to individual beneficiaries are taxed to them in the year they arise (the 23.5% in capital_gains), so paying that cash out costs nothing more; the family's EUR 400k a year is assumed to come from these distributions (the family realises about EUR 1.2 million of gains a year). Money taken out of the bucket company is a franked dividend: a top-rate shareholder pays 47% on the grossed-up dividend less the 30% franking credit, 24.3% of the cash dividend, less for family members on lower rates. Loans or payments from the company to the family without a dividend are deemed unfranked dividends under Division 7A unless made under a complying loan agreement.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Running cost is a reasoned estimate, not sourced: two tax returns and sets of accounts (trust and company), annual trustee distribution resolutions by 30 June, ASIC annual review fees for the trustee and bucket companies (a few hundred AUD each). The bucket company earns only passive income, so it pays 30%, not the 25% base-rate-entity rate (passive income above 80%). Division 7A (ITAA 1936) treats payments, loans and debt forgiveness by a private company to shareholders and associates as unfranked dividends unless a complying loan (benchmark interest, maximum 7 years unsecured) is put in place. The High Court held in Commissioner of Taxation v Bendel [2026] HCA 18 (10 June 2026) that an unpaid present entitlement owed by the trust to the bucket company is not by itself a Division 7A loan, but Subdivision EA (trust payments or loans to shareholders while an entitlement is unpaid), section 100A reimbursement agreements (distributions to adult children whose economic benefit goes to the parents: trustee taxed at 47%) and Part IVA remain. Distributions to minors are taxed at penalty rates on unearned income (Division 6AA, not verified here). Franked dividends need a family trust election and the 45-day holding rule for the credits to flow. Streaming of capital gains and franked dividends needs specific entitlement under the trust deed (Subdivisions 115-C and 207-B).
structure.exit_and_liquidation: If the family leaves Australia, individuals face CGT event I1 on assets that are not taxable Australian property (an election can defer it); trust and company remain Australian residents and keep being taxed in Australia, and unfranked or franked dividends to non-residents carry withholding tax. If the trustee or central management moves abroad the trust can cease to be resident (CGT event I2). Winding up the bucket company pays out retained profits as franked dividends; distributing trust assets in specie on vesting is a CGT event for the trust (E5/E7). Rules on exit from an opened source not verified in this session.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of the trust are streamed to individual beneficiaries, who keep the 50% CGT discount: 47% x 50% = 23.5% at the top rate (lower for adult children with little other income). Gains left to the bucket company would be taxed at 30% with no discount, so they are not streamed there.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Budget 2026-27 (12 May 2026): from 1 July 2027 the 50% discount is replaced by cost-base indexation and a 30% minimum tax for individuals and trusts on gains accruing after that date, and from 1 July 2028 discretionary trusts pay a minimum 30% tax. PwC describes the CGT change as a recent law change; legislative status of both measures not verified here. Not modelled.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Gains streamed to a top-rate individual: 45% + 2% Medicare levy = 47%, halved by the 50% discount for assets held at least 12 months = 23.5%, the same as direct holding. A company would pay 30% on the full gain (no discount). Law in force for disposals to 30 June 2027.
capital_gains.professional_trader: As standard: a trust that trades is taxed on revenue account, with no CGT discount.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains, with a foreign income tax offset for any foreign tax.

dividends.summary: Dividends are streamed to the bucket company and taxed there at 30%. Franked Australian dividends bear no further tax (the 30% franking credit offsets the 30% company tax). Foreign portfolio dividends are assessable to the company at 30% with a foreign income tax offset for withholding tax; the foreign-dividend exemption needs a 10% voting stake.
dividends.important_exceptions: Tax is deferred, not removed: paying the company's profits out to the family later costs 24.3% of the cash at the top rate. The announced 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts from 1 July 2028 would, according to professional commentary, give no credit to corporate beneficiaries, which would make streaming income to a bucket company through the trust double-taxed (not verified).

dividends.rate_basis: Company tax rate 30% (a passive investment company is not a base rate entity). Franked dividend D: taxable D/0.7, tax 30% x D/0.7 = 0.429D, less franking credit 0.429D = 0. Foreign dividends: 30% before the foreign income tax offset (typically 15% treaty withholding credited). Compared with 24.3% (franked) and 47% (foreign) for a top-rate individual.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Non-portfolio foreign dividends (10% or more of voting interests) are non-assessable non-exempt income for a company; portfolio dividends are not.

income.name: Australia

income_tax.summary: Residents pay 0% to AUD 18,200, then 15% (from 1 July 2026, down from 16%), 30% above AUD 45,000, 37% above AUD 135,000 and 45% above AUD 190,000, plus a 2% Medicare levy. There is no social security tax; employers pay 12% superannuation on top. Temporary visa holders are exempt on foreign-source income.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: The Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income applies to residents (surcharge of 1% to 1.5% without private hospital cover above income thresholds, not included). Superannuation at 12% is an employer cost for employees; PwC does not address compulsory super for the self-employed, so none is counted.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No state or municipal income tax. The tax-free threshold of AUD 18,200 is built into the brackets (0% band). Rates for 2025-26 were 16% on AUD 18,201-45,000. Low Income Tax Offset not included. The Medicare levy is recorded as the 'social security' rate, not in the brackets, to avoid double counting.
open_questions: Medicare levy low-income thresholds and surcharge thresholds not stated on the opened page.
From 1 July 2026 PwC reports a flat 'standard tax deduction' of up to AUD 1,000 for work-related expenses without substantiation; not modelled.

regimes.name: Temporary resident: foreign-source income exemption
regimes.description: A temporary visa holder who is not an Australian resident under the Social Security Act and has no Australian spouse is a temporary resident for tax and is exempt from Australian tax on foreign-source income (PwC residence page). It does not cover pay for work done in Australia: PwC states that foreign nationals are taxable on salary and allowances for services performed in Australia regardless of where the payment is made and whether it is remitted. A remote worker's salary or fees earned while living in Australia stay taxable, so the benefit is on passive foreign income.
regimes.duration_note: Applies while holding a temporary visa; length depends on the visa. No minimum income is a condition of the exemption (the Core Skills Income Threshold for the employer-sponsored 482 visa is AUD 79,423 from 1 July 2026, specialist stream AUD 146,576).

succession.name: Australia
succession.summary: A will can generally leave the estate to anyone, but each state and territory lets a court award provision to family and dependants who were left too little. Australia has trust law and the Hague Trusts Convention is in force. There is no private family foundation; only charitable structures exist.
succession.family_claims: Each state and territory has a family provision regime, e.g. NSW Succession Act 2006 Ch 3; Vic Administration and Probate Act 1958 Pt IV; Qld Succession Act 1981 Pt 4; WA Family Provision Act 1972; SA Inheritance (Family Provision) Act 1972 (now consolidated in the Succession Act 2023 (SA)); Tas Testators Family Maintenance Act 1912; ACT Family Provision Act 1969; NT Family Provision Act 1970. Eligible persons and the court's powers differ by state; claims can reach assets in a trust only in NSW through 'notional estate' orders.
succession.foreign_law_note: No choice of law by nationality. Succession to land follows the law of the place where it lies; succession to movables follows the deceased's last domicile (common-law conflict rules), so a foreign domiciliary's movables are governed by foreign law, but Australian land and family provision claims on Australian-domiciled estates are not avoided.
succession.trust_note: Convention in force for Australia since 1 Jan 1992 (ratified 17 Oct 1991). Trusts are governed by state Trusts/Trustee Acts and general law; foreign trusts are recognised. Trust income is taxed under the trust regime (Div 6 ITAA 1936), with special rules for non-resident trusts and the Foreign Resident CGT regime. There is no private foundation law; 'private ancillary funds' are charitable only.
open_questions: Confirm the 'notional estate' scope outside NSW and the exact family-provision statute section numbers per state.
Confirm whether the Convention covers external territories (Norfolk Island etc.); the HCCH table lists no extension.

immigration.name: Australia
immigration.summary: No free movement. EU, US and other passports face the same rules (some countries get visa-free or e-visa travel). Australia no longer sells residence: the Significant Investor Visa (AUD 5 million) closed to new applicants on 31 July 2024 and the retirement visa is repealed. The only elite route is the invitation-only National Innovation visa (subclass 858) for exceptional achievers. Everyone else needs an employer-sponsored visa such as the Skills in Demand 482. Australia has no digital nomad visa.
immigration.naturalisation: Citizenship by conferral needs 4 years of lawful residence in the 4 years before applying, the last 12 months as a permanent resident, good character, an English-language citizenship test; applicants aged 18 to 59 sit a citizenship test (pass mark 15 out of 20) (Home Affairs guidance).
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Australia allows dual citizenship; this was not confirmed on a page read in this run.

routes.summary: Invitation-only permanent visa for people with an internationally recognised record of exceptional achievement; it replaced Global Talent in December 2024.

routes.name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored temporary skilled work visa, with a Specialist Skills salary floor of AUD 146,717 and a Core Skills floor of AUD 79,499 from 1 July 2026.
routes.requirements: Employer sponsorship and a nominated occupation; Core Skills Income Threshold AUD 79,499 and Specialist Skills Income Threshold AUD 146,717 for applications from 1 July 2026 (AUD 76,515 and AUD 141,210 in 2025-26); one July 2026 alert reports slightly different figures (AUD 79,423 and AUD 146,576), so confirm with Home Affairs. Stay up to 4 years; permanent residence via the employer-sponsored 186 visa.
routes.physical_presence: Live and work in Australia for the sponsor
routes.family: Partner and dependants can be included.
